points.text: Intel's FY2025 10-K says that if it cannot secure a significant external foundry customer for Intel 14A it may pause or discontinue next-generation leading-edge nodes. It states it has been unsuccessful to date in securing any significant external foundry customers for any of its nodes, and that prospects for Intel 14A are uncertain [0000050863-26-000011:0065].

Intel says it has limited experience in the capital-intensive third-party foundry business and faces intense competition from TSMC, Samsung, Global Foundries, UMC and SMIC. It calls the hurdles to its foundry strategy highly risky with success highly uncertain, and notes it has delayed or cancelled projects in Ohio, Germany, Poland, Malaysia and Israel [0000050863-26-000011:0061].

Intel's high fixed cost structure means lower demand or inaccurate demand forecasting can disproportionately hurt gross margin and operating income. It recorded $950 million in 2025 and $3.3 billion in 2024 of non-cash impairment and accelerated depreciation charges on manufacturing assets [0000050863-26-000011:0064].

Intel reported R&D expenses of $13.8 billion in 2025, $16.5 billion in 2024 and $16.0 billion in 2023. It recognized Gaudi AI accelerator inventory-related charges of $375 million in 2025 and $922 million in 2024 after calling its Gaudi effort unsuccessful, and says it has been unsuccessful to date in becoming a meaningful participant in the AI GPU market [0000050863-26-000011:0062].

If Intel paused Intel 14A, its products business would over time depend on third-party foundries, particularly TSMC, with which it has no long-term contract. Only TSMC and Samsung currently produce the leading-edge nodes it needs, and competitors have longer relationships with them [0000050863-26-000011:0065]. The filings describe risks and do not give a view on whether to buy the shares.

Intel's FY2025 10-K says that on August 22, 2025 it entered a Warrant and Common Stock Agreement with the U.S. DOC. On August 27, 2025 it received the full remaining $5.7 billion of accelerated CHIPS Act disbursements, issued 275 million shares to the DOC, and issued a warrant for up to 241 million shares at $20.00 per share, exercisable if Intel ceased to own at least 51% of Intel Foundry [0000050863-26-000011:0030].

Intel put 159 million shares into escrow, to be released to the U.S. government at $20.00 per share as Intel receives the $3.2 billion of Secure Enclave disbursements. As of December 27, 2025, 3 million escrowed shares had been released. The amended CHIPS Act agreement removed prior project milestone requirements and substantially all other conditions to disbursement [0000050863-26-000011:0030].

Intel's FY2025 MD&A says it entered two private placement share sale agreements in Q3 2025 to support strategic investments in advanced manufacturing, AI infrastructure and long-term growth initiatives. This describes how Intel is funding its strategy, not whether the shares are a good buy [0000050863-26-000011:0030].

In its FY2024 10-K, Intel said it suspended quarterly dividends starting in Q4 2024 and agreed under its CHIPS Act agreement to forgo dividends for two years, with limits on dividends for three years after that. It does not expect dividends or stock repurchases until its cash flows improve. Its last repurchase was in Q1 2021 [0000050863-25-000009:0010].

Intel's FY2024 risk factors warn that its Smart Capital approach, alternative financing and pursuit of government grants may not succeed. They also say Intel may not build a competitive foundry business for external customers, which would make it hard to earn a return on its process technology and capacity investments. Intel recognized a $755 million charge in Q4 2024 for expected Ireland SCIP penalties [0000050863-25-000009:0054].

Intel's FY2025 10-K describes a multi-year strategy with four priorities: transforming its culture, revitalizing the x86 ecosystem, growing its external foundry business, and expanding market opportunities through purpose-built ASICs and GPUs for AI workloads [0000050863-26-000011:0006].

On culture and finance, Intel says that in 2025 it simplified its organizational structure, reduced management layers, aligned capital investments with customer demand signals and continued to monetize non-core assets. It describes the cultural transformation as ongoing and these changes as foundational steps [0000050863-26-000011:0006].

Intel announced a strategic partnership with NVIDIA to co-develop custom client and data center products combining Intel x86 CPUs with NVIDIA's AI and accelerated computing capabilities, intended to span multiple product generations for hyperscale, enterprise and consumer markets [0000050863-26-000011:0006][0000050863-26-000011:0007].

Intel says it released its first Intel Core Ultra Series 3 processors in 2025, the first products built on its Intel 18A process, and expects 18A to serve multiple generations of future client and server CPUs. It is also developing Intel 14A, designed from inception for external customers [0000050863-26-000011:0007].

The excerpts describe strategy and progress only and give no basis for investment advice. Intel says its competitiveness depends on access to leading-edge manufacturing capacity and advanced packaging, and that its cultural transformation is still ongoing, so the excerpts do not say whether now is a good time to buy INTC shares [0000050863-26-000011:0006][0000050863-26-000011:0007].

Intel's FY2025 10-K says it is developing Intel 14A and seeking a significant external customer for it; if it cannot secure one and meet customer milestones, it may pause or discontinue Intel 14A and successor nodes and various manufacturing expansion projects, since they may not be economical [0000050863-26-000011:0034][0000050863-26-000011:0021].

Intel's FY2025 10-K describes footprint actions in 2025: consolidating Costa Rican assembly and test into sites in Vietnam and Malaysia, slowing construction of the Ohio fab, and discontinuing planned expansions in Germany (fab) and Poland (assembly and test) to align capital spending with market demand [0000050863-26-000011:0034][0000050863-26-000011:0008].

Intel says it has few external foundry customers to date, though growing the external foundry business is a key long-term strategy. Leading-edge node cost structures require wafer volumes beyond what its own products are expected to provide [0000050863-26-000011:0008][0000050863-26-000011:0021].

Intel 18A went into high-volume manufacturing in late 2025 and is used for the first Intel Core Ultra Series 3 processor. Intel expects 18A and its derivative 18A-P to be the key process for multiple generations of future client and server CPUs, and it is seeking to make 18A its first significant foundry node [0000050863-26-000011:0021].

If Intel discontinued Intel 14A and successor nodes, it expects most products to keep being made in its own facilities on nodes up to Intel 18A-P through at least 2030. It would shift manufacturing over time to third-party foundries, particularly TSMC, for nodes beyond 18A and 18A-P [0000050863-26-000011:0034][0000050863-26-000011:0008].

questions.question: Beyond lost direct sales, what knock-on competitive effects of U.S.-China export controls and trade tensions do NVIDIA, AMD and Intel describe in their latest 10-Ks?

answer.text:
NVIDIA says export controls have a disproportionate impact on it and may disadvantage it against competitors selling chips outside the controls' scope [0001045810-26-000021:0044][0001045810-26-000021:0045]. It says the controls have encouraged customers to "design-out" certain U.S. semiconductors, and overseas governments to ask customers to buy from competitors rather than NVIDIA [0001045810-26-000021:0045].
It says this helped competitors build larger developer and customer ecosystems to challenge it worldwide [0001045810-26-000021:0042][0001045810-26-000021:0014].

It also says its competitive position has been harmed and will be harmed further if restrictions persist or expand, if customers buy from competitors or develop internal solutions, or if licenses are delayed [0001045810-26-000021:0043].
It has also discouraged them from buying, importing or using NVIDIA data center products, including China-specific products designed to comply with U.S. rules [0001045810-26-000021:0045]. Chinese regulators published a preliminary finding on September 15, 2025 that NVIDIA's compliance with U.S. export controls violated the terms of China's approval of its Mellanox acquisition, which could bring penalties or restrictions [0001045810-26-000021:0015][0001045810-26-000021:0041].
Controls have hurt and may hurt demand in Europe, Latin America and Southeast Asia, and may increase investment in foreign competitors less likely to be restricted [0001045810-26-000021:0045]. They can also disrupt supply chains and distribution channels, including for non-data-center products [0001045810-26-000021:0045][0001045810-26-000021:0041]. The possibility of further controls has already reduced demand, benefiting competitors with alternatives less likely to be restricted, and can leave NVIDIA with excess inventory and purchase obligations, as with the H20 [0001045810-26-000021:0041][0001045810-26-000021:0045].

answer.text:
Pillar Two imposes a minimum effective corporate tax rate, and NVIDIA says its tax obligations and effective tax rate could increase as a result [0001045810-26-000021:0051]. It says a number of countries where it does business have enacted, or are enacting, elements of Pillar Two, including the recently released "side-by-side" framework with additional safe harbors and coordination mechanisms [0001045810-26-000021:0051]. It says Pillar Two changes, including those related to the side-by-side framework, may increase tax uncertainty and compliance costs and adversely affect its provision for income taxes, cash tax payments, results of operations and financial condition [0001045810-26-000021:0052][0001045810-26-000021:0051]. The excerpts give no dollar or percentage estimate, so NVIDIA has not quantified the impact there [0001045810-26-000021:0052].

Many countries have enacted Pillar Two-based laws effective from 2024, though some jurisdictions where AMD operates have not yet adopted them [0000002488-26-000018:0079]. It says it continues to evaluate the effect of proposed and enacted changes on its effective tax rate and cash flows [0000002488-26-000018:0079]. AMD calls these rules generally favorable but says each country must adopt them before they are enacted for financial accounting purposes [0000002488-26-000018:0046][0000002488-26-000018:0079]. AMD describes the impact as immaterial for 2024 and 2025 [0000002488-26-000018:0079], and NVIDIA gives no estimate [0001045810-26-000021:0052].

questions.question: How does dependence on external foundries, and on TSMC in particular, differ across NVIDIA, AMD and Intel according to their latest 10-K risk factors?

answer.text:
It relies on TSMC for all microprocessor and GPU wafers at 7 nm or smaller nodes and primarily on GF for larger nodes [0000002488-26-000018:0029]. AMD says it is focusing its 7 nm and lower microprocessor and GPU portfolio on TSMC's processes, and that its business could be materially adversely affected if TSMC cannot make enough wafers at those nodes to meet demand [0000002488-26-000018:0032]. It also says TSMC manufactures its newest IC products, and that it relies on TSMC, UMC and its other foundries [0000002488-26-000018:0032]. AMD warns that foundry yield problems or delayed transitions to advanced process technologies could raise unit costs, hurt gross margin or force it to allocate supply among customers [0000002488-26-000018:0032]. questions.question: How do NVIDIA, AMD and Intel each describe the role of their software and developer ecosystems in competing for AI and computing workloads, according to their latest 10-Ks?

Intel: Intel says x86 client CPUs are the foundational PC platform, which has enabled a deep and extensive software ecosystem [0000050863-26-000011:0011]. Intel defines oneAPI as an open, cross-architecture programming model allowing a single code base across multiple architectures, though the excerpt does not describe its competitive role [0000050863-26-000011:0180].
